warnings.message: Current NEFF is missing compiler metrics. Please re-compile using latest version of the compiler

Missing HLO stats in the NEFF, `model_flops` and `mfu_hlo_estimated_percent` summary metrics will not be available. Consider the metrics (hardware_flops - transpose_flops) and mfu_inst_estimated_percent instead.

metric_schema.field_description: Number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) performed by this instruction. Each MAC (multiply-accumulate) operation counts as 2 FLOPs (one multiply, one add). Note that as each FP32 matmul lowers to two FP32_LO_HI instructions, each FP32_LO_HI matmul records half the logical FLOPs.

metric_schema.field_description: BF16-equivalent FLOPs for this instruction. Scales FLOPs to the BF16 throughput equivalent so the result can be used with BF16 peak throughput as the denominator for PE utilization calculations. BF16, FP16, and TF32 use a 1.0x multiplier. FP32 uses 4.0x. On Trn2/Trn3, FP8@FP8 and UINT8@UINT8 matmuls use 0.5x; FP8 or UINT8 mixed with a higher-precision operand uses 1.0x (executes at BF16 throughput). FP8 uses 1.0x on Trn1/Inf2. MXFP8 and MXFP4 use 0.25x on Trn3.

caveats: Use unprofiled same-host phase runs for speed; traces are attribution.
Runtime API durations contain asynchronous queueing and overlap.
Source/engine activity unions overlap and are not additive wall-time shares.
Dropped EVENT/DMA warnings can mean missing instructions or inaccurate counters; absence is not proof of no work.
Missing dynamic DMA metadata prevents exact traffic or bandwidth claims.
Sampled SBUF utilization is not a complete allocator/live-memory proof.
BF16-cost multipliers follow the installed Explorer schema, not assumed FLOP peaks.
